claims.explanation: NSC-663284 is a quinone-based Cdc25 inhibitor that also redox cycles to generate reactive oxygen species, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on Cdc25A/B/C and/or sensitivity to oxidative stress. Tumors with BRAF or RAS pathway activation and PTEN loss may be more reliant on Cdc25-mediated cell cycle progression and less able to buffer oxidative stress, while intact KEAP1/NFE2L2 antioxidant signaling and certain lineage contexts confer protection.

features.basis: Observed enrichment of BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma and other lines; BRAF-driven tumors may depend on Cdc25 for G1/S and G2/M progression.
Observed in multiple sensitive lines; PTEN loss increases PI3K/AKT signaling and may enhance dependence on Cdc25 and oxidative stress sensitivity.
Observed in sensitive lines; RAS pathway activation may increase reliance on Cdc25 phosphatases for cell cycle progression.
Observed in several sensitive lines; KRAS-driven tumors may be more dependent on Cdc25 and susceptible to redox-based inhibition.
Observed in a sensitive endometrial line; KEAP1 loss impairs antioxidant response, potentially increasing sensitivity to ROS generated by NSC-663284.
Observed in a sensitive endometrial line; NFE2L2 mutations can dysregulate antioxidant response, possibly enhancing ROS-mediated killing.
NSC-663284 directly inhibits Cdc25A (Ki 29 nM); high expression may predict greater dependence and sensitivity.
NSC-663284 is most selective for Cdc25B (Ki 95 nM); high expression may predict sensitivity.
NSC-663284 inhibits Cdc25C (Ki 89 nM); high expression may predict sensitivity.
Observed in several sensitive lines; NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling, potentially increasing Cdc25 dependence.
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so not a strong predictor; however, some resistant lines have TP53 mutations, suggesting context-dependent effects.
Observed in several resistant lines; ATM loss may impair DNA damage response and reduce sensitivity to cell cycle checkpoint inhibition.
